title: Rule list (yg aspects --json)
$comment: This schema describes exactly what this release of Yggdrasil writes: every mapping is closed and every enumeration lists only the values this release uses. Use it to check a producer. Do not use it to reject a document you read: under the family rule a later release may add a field or a value within /1, and a /1 reader ignores what it does not know (see family-contracts).

kind.description: Reviewer kind: a judged rule, a local check, or a bundle with no reviewer of its own.

tier.description: The reviewer tier a judged rule resolves to, when it names one.

status.description: The rule's own default status; an attach site may raise it per component.

reviewBy.description: The standing request to re-examine whether the rule still earns its place, as a bare `YYYY-MM-DD` date. Null when the rule names none.

errs.description: The rule's honest error direction, on a local check that declares one.

reach.description: Every subject the rule reaches, named rather than counted — present ONLY when the caller asked for it with `--reach`. Absent by default, so the document a caller already reads stays byte-identical to what it was before this field existed, and nobody pays the enumeration who did not ask for it.

log.description: The last thing the rule's own history recorded — so a reader of this document does not have to open files to know whether a rule has been touched, when, and whether its standing moved.

at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp of the newest entry, or null when there is none.

statusChange.description: The standing the newest entry recorded, when it recorded one.

unit.description: The subject: one component, or one file governed by its architecture type.

node.description: The owning component, or null for a file no component owns.

status.description: Effective status on THIS subject — the standing that decides whether a finding blocks here, which an attach site may raise above the rule's own default. A `draft` unit is listed like any other: a rule that reaches nothing and a rule that reaches ten subjects it is not yet judging are different facts, and an empty list must only ever mean the first.

via.description: Which channel delivered the rule here.

from.description: Where it came from, when the channel has an origin to name: the ancestor component (`hierarchy`), the architecture type (`architecture`, `type`), the flow (`flow`), the port and the component publishing it (`port`), the rule that implies this one (`implied`). Null for `own`, whose origin is the subject itself.

nodes.description: Components where the rule is effective, however it got there.

architecture.description: Attached by an architecture type's defaults.

inherited.description: Declared on an ancestor component (or an ancestor's architecture type) and inherited down the hierarchy.

port.description: Required by a port the component consumes.

implied.description: Pulled in ONLY by another rule's `implies` — no attachment of its own reaches the component.

flow.description: Propagated from a flow the component participates in.

typeCovered.description: Files governed by an architecture type alone, with no component of their own.
